## About
ABC Animal Clinic and Hospital sits in Downtown Fort Worth's Medical District on South Freeway. It started as a low cost spay and neuter clinic and has grown into a full service veterinary hospital, while keeping the affordable clinic atmosphere it began with.
The focus is disease prevention, maintenance and treatment, delivered with compassionate and professional care. Just as important is keeping you informed. As the clinic puts it, client education is the first line of defense in managing the health and well being of your pet.
One longtime client says Dr. Snodgrass explains things in a way that makes even stressful situations feel manageable. The clinic is open Monday through Saturday, and visits are by appointment.

## Services
- Preventative Care Examinations: A yearly exam with immunizations and testing is what the clinic recommends to keep your pet healthy. ($25)
- Medical Examinations: For a pet who is sick, hurt or just not right. By appointment. ($75)
- Pre-Surgical Examinations: Required before any anesthetic procedure. This visit is also how you get a detailed estimate for surgery or dental work. ($55)
- Spays and neuters: Where ABC got its start. Prices differ for cats and dogs, and the Pre-Surgical Examination fee is separate. Call for current rates.
- Dental Cleanings: Recommended every year, or sooner if the veterinarian advises, to help prevent or control periodontal disease. (Cleanings start at $120)
- In-House Diagnostics (Including Digital X-rays): Lab work done in the clinic while you wait, plus digital X-ray imaging to help diagnose illness or injury quickly and accurately. Call for imaging prices.
- On-site Pharmacy: A wide range of medications kept in stock, so your pet's treatment can start without a wait or a second trip.
- Boarding: A place for your pets to stay while you're away. Reservations go through the appointment scheduler. Call for rates and policies.

## FAQ
Q: Do I need an appointment?
A: Yes. All office visits are by appointment only, and there are additional charges for emergencies and walk-ins.

Q: Why is the front door closed on Mondays and Saturdays?
A: On those days the front door is open only for boarding and medication pick ups. Please call the clinic for refill requests, pick ups and drop offs.

Q: Does my pet need an exam before surgery?
A: Yes. A Pre-Surgical Examination is required before any procedure that involves anesthesia, and it is also when you get a detailed estimate.

Q: How do drop off and pick up work for surgery?
A: Bring your pet in the evening before the surgery date. Most patients can go home the following day between 3:30 PM and 5 PM.

Q: Should I bring a stool sample?
A: Please do. As the clinic says, scoop the poop. Fresh samples give better results and are easier on your pet.
